decision.recommended_change: Do not keep the intersecting source faces as a protected exterior. Rebuild only the hidden underarm fold patch bounded by the listed implicated source faces, preserving its boundary vertices and the visible silhouette; then regenerate the inner shell.
decision.design_boundary: Treat this as a bad imported underarm fold, not as an approved visible design feature: the exact crossings are wholly inside two retained source-face patches. Preserve each patch boundary and matched exterior silhouette; change only the hidden patch tessellation/interior coordinates needed to remove the crossing.
decision.protected_scope: No approved exterior coordinates should change unless the outer-source exact self-intersection test is nonzero or every nonzero local offset fails.
risk: A global thickness reduction weakens the cloth cue everywhere and is not the smallest change.
Deleting underarm faces without rebuilding a bounded manifold patch would create holes and break the closed tissue.
Body-proxy collisions are a separate provisional-body issue and do not diagnose this cloth-shell failure.
verification_plan: Re-run exact outer self-intersection: require zero non-neighbor proper/edge/coplanar intersections.
Re-run exact inner-vs-outer intersection: require zero true intersections; BVH candidate count alone is not the gate.
Require closed manifold robe tissue with zero boundary/nonmanifold edges and unchanged four opening rings.
Render the existing front/back/side/quarter and cuff/underhem views; compare silhouette and approved exterior against v2.
decision.stop_condition: Stop once exact outer self-intersection and exact outer-inner intersection are both zero, manifold/opening checks remain unchanged, and matched views show no approved exterior silhouette change. Do not broaden into full-character retopology or body-proxy repair.
